title: Generic termal-test-state root remains after a green Rust suite; attribute its owner and explain cleanup refusal
outcome: Attribute and repair the fixture lifetime or harness behavior that left a generic termal-test-state root after the original green Rust suite. Keep cleanup strict and make a refusal name the creator when retained evidence provides it, with an explicit reason when attribution is unavailable.
acceptance: The reported leftover is attributed to its fixture and late accessor or cleanup owner, and a behavioral regression verifies that the repaired owner preserves cleanup through the last access without weakening the temp guard.
A cleanup refusal reports the creating test or owner when that information is available, and explains why attribution is unavailable otherwise; it preserves the failed run's evidence.
